challenges.name: normalization-quiz
challenges.title: Copies that drift and columns that depend on part of the key
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the renamed-course incident: the drift query after a quick fix, and a progress table that copies the lesson title. Decide whether each statement is True or False.

questions.question:
enrollments(user_id, course_id, course_title, enrolled_at, status), primary key (user_id, course_id). course_title is copied from courses.title when a learner enrolls.

After course 12 was renamed, the drift query returns:

course_id | copied_title | current_title       | rows
----------+--------------+---------------------+-----
12        | SQL Basics   | SQL & Data Modeling | 412

A teammate proposes to run once:

UPDATE enrollments
SET course_title = (SELECT title FROM courses WHERE courses.id = enrollments.course_id);

Statement: "After this UPDATE, the schema is fixed: course titles in enrollments can no longer drift from courses."
questions.explanation: False. The UPDATE repairs the rows that exist today, so the drift query returns nothing for now. The design is unchanged: the title is still stored in every enrollment row, so the next rename (or a new code path that inserts an enrollment with a stale title) drifts again. This is the update anomaly of a 2NF violation, since course_title depends only on course_id. The fix is to remove the copy and read courses.title through a join, or, if a copy is really needed, give it one owner such as a trigger plus a reconcile query.

questions.question:
A teammate designs the progress table like this:

CREATE TABLE lesson_progress (
  user_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  lesson_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES lessons(id),
  completed_at TEXT    NOT NULL,
  lesson_title TEXT    NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, lesson_id)
);

Statement: "lesson_title depends on lesson_id alone, not on the whole key (user_id, lesson_id), so this table is not in second normal form."
questions.explanation: True. With a composite key, second normal form asks every non-key column to depend on the whole key. completed_at needs both parts (when this learner finished this lesson), but lesson_title is the same for every learner of a lesson: it depends on lesson_id only. That partial dependency means the title is repeated in every progress row and will drift when a lesson is renamed, exactly like course_title in enrollments. A common misconception is that a table is normalized as long as it has a primary key; the question is what each column depends on.
